sources.note: Bibliographic only: zero descriptive references for Leti; only Dieu & Renaud 1983 and Binam Bikoi (ed.) 2012 (ALCAM inventories) are coded [leo]. Glottolog comment: Leti is the ancestral language of the Mengisa (who shift to Eton) and 'is so close to Tuki [bag] as to perhaps count as a dialect of it (Biloa 2013: 37-38)'.
Irrelevant: these six IGT rows are Leti of Southwest Maluku (Austronesian, van Engelenhoven), mis-assigned to leti1245.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. LOT Dissertation Series 410. Utrecht: LOT. 413 pp.
sources.note: Nothing for Leti. Leti appears only in the introduction and classification chapter: p.8-9 + fn.13 (the Mengisa speak two languages, Njowi ~ Eton/Ewondo and Leti ~ Tuki; 100-word lexicostatistics Leti 82-84% with Tuki-Tocenga/Tutsingo), fn.23 (Leti = 'Tungijo', considered by Tuki speakers a dialect of Tuki, citing Kongne Welaze 2004: 8-9 and Dieu & Renaud 1983: 108-109), pp.364-365 + fn.305 (A.63 Mengisa [Leti]; 'Leti is most definitely an A60 language and is often considered a dialect of Tuki'). Leti is not among the ten Mbam languages described.

sources.citation: Kongne Welaze, Jacquis, et al. 2008 [rev. of 2005/2006]. Precis d'orthographe pour la langue tuki. Yaounde: SIL Cameroun. 17 pp.
sources.note: Tuki [bag] only, based on the Tutsingo dialect; lists dialects Tukombe, Tocenga, Tutsingo, Tonjo, Tungoro, Tumbele (Leti/Tungijo not included). Sec. 3 'Les tons': H and L lexical tones (M derived from lowered H), contour tones only on long vowels, grammatical meanings 'rendues uniquement par des tons'. No statement about stress/accent.
Nothing on stress; Leti 'quite close to Tuki and may be a dialect'; Tuki page lists Leti/Mengisa as a possible dialect and cites Essono 1974 for Tuki segmental phonology.
